trust_decision.summary: Whether an already-installed registry pack may be trusted (its profile merged, its lockfile-listed artifacts used, the sandbox built and the pack dir granted read) is decided by verify_profile_packs; at the pinned commit that check only hashes artifacts when a lockfile entry exists and only checks signer/provenance when a .nono-trust.bundle exists, so absent metadata returns Ok instead of failing.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'registry pack verification can fail open when provenance metadata is absent', and this is the only run-time re-verification of an installed pack: `let locked = lockfile.packages.get(pack_ref); if let Some(locked_pkg) = locked { ... }` makes the whole artifact-hash loop conditional on the lockfile entry existing.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: crates/nono-cli/src/wiring.rs:326-405 (execute -> execute_one WriteFile ownership guard; fix relaxes it via the new pub execute_with_options/ExecuteOptions)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the advisory is only about pack provenance verification, that refuse-to-overwrite-a-user-file in the wiring interpreter is a pre-existing, unrelated safety check, and that `nono pull --force` recovery is a CLI convenience - so they never add the force plumbing or the identical-content exception.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After losing local package metadata, `nono pull <ref> --force` must still be able to adopt a destination file that already exists and is byte-identical to the pack source, while a user-edited managed file and a different-content unmanaged file are still refused; a flat fail-closed verification (or a force flag that overwrites anything) breaks one half or the other.

O6_input_shapes: pack install dir present with no lockfile entry at all (lockfile deleted or pack dir copied in; read_lockfile returns Lockfile::default())
lockfile entry present but provenance absent (serde default -> Option::None from an older/hand-edited lockfile)
lockfile entry + provenance present but .nono-trust.bundle missing
lockfile entry present with an empty artifacts map (no hashes to check)
WriteFile dest exists, unmanaged, content identical to pack source, under --force (must be adopted)
WriteFile dest exists, unmanaged, content differs (must still be refused)
WriteFile dest exists, managed but edited since install (must still be refused)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Pack-provided policy groups.json is merged into the global policy for every key in the lockfile with no hash, bundle or signer check, at load_embedded_policy time
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Groups are read from packs already listed in the lockfile and pulled once with a verified bundle, so the lockfile entry is treated as the trust anchor - exactly the assumption the advisory breaks.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another module of the same crate (policy.rs vs profile_runtime.rs), reached through load_embedded_policy which verify_profile_packs never calls

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `nono why --profile <ns>/<name>` builds CapabilitySet::from_profile and the allowed-domain set straight from the pack profile without ever calling verify_profile_packs
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: why is a read-only explain command; it prints what would be allowed and never creates a sandbox, so verification is argued to be a run-time concern.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file away from the landing point, different module (why_runtime.rs)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: load_registry_profile reads package.json and profiles/<install_as>.json out of an installed pack before any verification, and the inspection commands stop there via load_profile_no_migrate
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: profile show/diff/validate only display the file and never execute the pack, so the solver ignores the pack-loading path and fixes only the run-time check.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module of the same crate (profile/mod.rs), reached from profile_cmd.rs:864 and profile_cmd.rs:1337

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second per-artifact integrity gate for groups.json before it is merged into policy.groups
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The loop already reads arbitrary installed pack content keyed only by a lockfile name; a maintainer hardening 'pack content must be verified before use' would naturally add the same lockfile/bundle check here, especially since verify_profile_packs only covers packs named by the active profile.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An ownership/identical-content guard on the `--init` instruction copy into the user's project CWD
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: copy_instruction_to_project (package_cmd.rs:955-962) writes pack content into the user's tree and only checks existence, so the identical-content-adoption logic the fix adds for WriteFile has an obvious sibling here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Per-directive 'do not touch a file this pack did not create' option for JsonMerge / JsonArrayAppend / TomlBlock / YamlMerge, mirroring the WriteFile option
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Those directives write into user-owned config files by design and carry only reversal records, so a maintainer extending the new ExecuteOptions pattern could add the same guard there.
